'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**[[Mainok attack]]
***[[ISWAP]] [[jihadist]]s attack an [[Nigerian Army|army]] convoy and [[military base|base]] in Mainok, [[Borno State]], [[Nigeria]], killing at least 31 soldiers. [https://guardian.ng/news/jihadists-kill-31-soldiers-in-northeast-nigeria/ (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Makurdi kidnapping]]
**Gunmen [[kidnap]] students from the Federal University of Agriculture in [[Makurdi]], [[Benue State]], Nigeria. [https://guardian.ng/news/gunmen-abduct-benue-university-students/ (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**Two [[Spain|Spanish]] journalists and an [[Ireland|Irish]] campaigner are killed after their convoy is attacked in eastern [[Burkina Faso]]. Two Burkinabe soldiers are wounded. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/27/two-spanish-citizens-killed-in-burkina-faso-ambush (''Al Jazeera'')]
**At least 18 civilians are killed after militants attack the village of Yattakou, in Burkina Faso. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/29/at-least-18-killed-in-northern-burkina-faso-attack-by-gunmen (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Karnataka]], [[COVID-19 lockdown in India]]
*****The [[Government of Karnataka|state government]] announces a two week lockdown across [[Karnataka]] from April 27 at 9:00 p.m. until May 12 at 6:00 a.m. [[Indian Standard Time|IST]]. Additionally, only essential shops would be allowed to operate from 6:00 a.m. until 10:00 a.m. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/karnataka/karnataka-govt-announces-lockdown-for-14-days/article34414226.ece (''The Hindu'')]
****[[India]] reports 352,991 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, a world record for the fifth consecutive day, and thereby bringing the total number of confirmed cases to 17.3 million. The country also reports a record 2,812 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 195,123. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/india-covid-cases-record-5th-day-volunteers-find-oxygen-hospital-beds/ (CBS News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports a record 496 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 70,070. [https://www.tasnimnews.com/en/news/2021/04/26/2492001/covid-daily-death-toll-in-iran-sets-new-record-soars-past-490 (Tasnim News Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] surpasses 10,000 deaths of COVID-19. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2021/04/701902612a7d-urgent-japans-covid-19-death-toll-tops-10000-amid-3rd-virus-emergency.html (Kyodo News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****[[Pakistan]] surpasses 800,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://www.thenews.com.pk/amp/826368-pakistan-crosses-800000-mark-with (''The News International'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] surpasses one million cases of COVID-19. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/news/04/26/21/philippines-covid19-cases-1-million-april262021 (ABS-CBN News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education]]
****Nursery and primary schools reopens in [[France]] after a three-week closure in the first step of the partial [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] easing. [https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210426-covid-19-schools-reopen-across-france-despite-spike-in-icu-admissions (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] reopens bars, restaurants, cinemas, and concert halls as three-quarters of the [[Regions of Italy|regions]] are placed in the low-risk "yellow zone" categories. [https://www.euractiv.com/section/coronavirus/news/finally-italy-reopens-as-parliament-debates-recovery-plan/ (''Euractiv'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****The [[Netherlands]] bans all passenger flights from [[India]] until May 1 due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases in India. [https://www.dutchnews.nl/news/2021/04/dutch-ban-passenger-flights-from-india-on-public-health-institute-advice/ (DutchNews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Norway]]
****[[Norway|Norwegian]] [[Prime Minister of Norway|Prime Minister]] [[Erna Solberg]] receives her first dose of the [[Moderna]] [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/norways-prime-minister-gets-covid-19-vaccine-2021-04-26/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey|Turkish]] [[President of Turkey|President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] announces a full lockdown from April 29 until May 17 in an attempt to reduce the spread of COVID-19. Under the new restrictions, all workplaces, except for those excluded by the [[Ministry of Interior (Turkey)|Interior Ministry]], will be closed, intercity travel will be subject to permission and public transportation will operate at only 50% capacity. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/covid-19-turkey-announces-full-lockdown-from-thursday-/2221503# (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Brunswick]], [[Lineage B.1.617]]
****[[New Brunswick]] reports its first case of the Lineage B.1.617 variant, which was originally detected in [[India]]. [https://globalnews.ca/news/7810521/new-brunswick-covid-19-variant-india/amp/ (Global News)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***The [[Bio E COVID-19]] vaccine, developed by [[Biological E. Limited]] and the [[Baylor College of Medicine]], enters phase III of clinical trials at the [[Texas Children's Hospital]] in [[Houston]]. [https://www.miragenews.com/biological-e-limited-to-begin-phase-iii-549792/ (Mirage News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Egypt–Turkey relations]], [[Libyan peace process]]
**A [[Turkish government]] spokesman says they are working on improving ties with the [[Egyptian government]] in order to boost efforts in the Libyan peace process. Relations between the two countries have been strained since the [[2013 Egyptian coup d'état]] due to close relations between Turkey and the [[Muslim Brotherhood]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/turkey-says-better-ties-with-cairo-could-boost-libya-peace-efforts-2021-04-26/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*A court in [[Russia]] orders the [[Anti-Corruption Foundation]], linked to [[opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia|opposition]] leader and activist [[Alexei Navalny]], to cease its activities. Navalny's ally [[Leonid Volkov (politician)|Leonid Volkov]] explains that the ruling forbids the Foundation from publishing anything online, taking part in elections, and organizing protests. The ruling comes after [[prosecutor]]s sought to label the group as "[[extremist]]s". [https://www.dw.com/en/russia-suspends-activities-of-alexei-navalnys-campaign-groups/a-57335053 (Deutsche Welle)]
*[[Ministry of Industry (Spain)|Spanish Minister of Industry, Trade and Tourism]] [[Reyes Maroto]] receives an envelope containing a bloody knife, thereby becoming the second [[government of Spain|minister]] and the fourth senior politician to receive death threats. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/spanish-minister-sent-red-stained-knife-after-death-threats-others-2021-04-26/ (Reuters)]
*More than 1,300 prisoners in [[Burundi]] are released after [[President of Burundi|President]] [[Évariste Ndayishimiye]] [[pardon]]ed nearly 5,000 prisoners in March to reduce the [[prison overcrowding|overcrowding of the country's prisons]]. [https://www.channelstv.com/2021/04/26/burundi-frees-1300-prisoners-under-presidential-pardon/ (Channels TV)]
*[[Iranians in the United Kingdom|British Iranian]] national [[Nazanin Zaghari-Ratcliffe]] is sentenced to one year in prison and is barred from leaving Iran for a further year over propaganda activities against the [[Government of Iran|government]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/british-iranian-zaghari-ratcliffe-sentenced-to-a-year-in-prison-lawyer (Radio France Internationale)]
*[[Argentina|Argentine]] Cardinal [[Leonardo Sandri]], the Prefect of the [[Congregation for the Oriental Churches]], states that the [[Armenian Genocide|Armenian genocide]] is a ‘stain’ of evil on all humanity. An estimated 1.5 million Armenians were killed in the genocide. [https://www.catholicnewsagency.com/news/247402/vatican-cardinal-the-armenian-genocide-is-a-stain-of-evil-on-all-humanity (Catholic News Agency)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2020 United States census]], [[2020 United States redistricting cycle]]
**The [[United States Census Bureau]] announces the [[United States|country]]'s total population to be over 331 million people, thereby marking the second-slowest growth rate in its history. It also announces that [[Texas]] will gain two congressional seats during the redistricting process, with [[Colorado]], [[Florida]], [[Montana]], [[North Carolina]], and [[Oregon]] gaining one seat each; [[California]], [[Illinois]], [[Michigan]], [[New York (state)|New York]], [[Ohio]], [[Pennsylvania]], and [[West Virginia]] will each lose a seat. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/04/26/politics/us-census-2020-results/index.html (CNN)]
